title: Vocabulary Quiz: 20 English Words to Test You
description: Test your English vocabulary with 20 free questions on word meanings, synonyms, and antonyms. Easy to expert levels, with an explanation after each answer.
h1: Vocabulary Quiz: How Strong Is Your English?
intro: Words are powerful, and a rich vocabulary helps you read, write, and speak with confidence. This vocabulary quiz asks 20 questions about the meanings of English words, along with synonyms and antonyms. The first eight use everyday words, the middle eight introduce more advanced terms you might meet in books and news, and the last four are tough words that even confident readers can find tricky. You get about five seconds per question, and every answer comes with a short explanation and often an example. It's free, quick, and good for students, writers, and word lovers. Let's see how many words you really know!

questions.q: Which word means the same as "enormous"?
questions.explication: Enormous describes something extremely large, such as an enormous mountain or an enormous crowd.
Ancient means very old, especially from the distant past, while modern describes something recent or current.
A brief meeting lasts only a short time. It can also mean using few words.
A stingy person is unwilling to spend or give, while a generous person gives freely.
Gales are strong enough to break tree branches and make walking difficult.
Owls, bats, and hedgehogs are nocturnal animals.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for "weary"?
questions.explication: Weary means worn out, either physically or from boredom or worry.

choices: A piece of land planted with fruit trees
questions.explication: Apples, cherries, and peaches are often grown in orchards.

choices: Lasting for a very short time
questions.explication: A rainbow or a soap bubble is ephemeral. The word comes from a Greek term meaning "lasting a day."

questions.q: Which word best describes someone who is "benevolent"?
questions.explication: A benevolent donor, for example, gives money to help others.

choices: A person who is very funny
A person who is always in a hurry
A person who says very little
questions.explication: Taciturn people tend to be reserved and speak only when necessary.

choices: Careful about spending money or using resources
questions.explication: A frugal person avoids waste. Frugal can also describe a plain, inexpensive meal.
Smartphones have become ubiquitous, meaning you see them everywhere.

choices: A word that sounds like its meaning
A mild word used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one
questions.explication: Saying someone "passed away" instead of "died" is a euphemism.

questions.q: A statement that is "ambiguous" is one that…
choices: Can be understood in more than one way
questions.explication: The sentence "I saw her duck" is ambiguous because duck could be a bird or an action.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for "candid"?
questions.explication: A candid answer is honest and direct, even if it is not what the listener hopes to hear.

choices: A person who flatters others to gain advantage
questions.explication: The word comes from a Greek term for an informer. Today it means a flatterer or "yes-man."

choices: A job that pays well but requires little work
questions.explication: The word comes from Latin sine cura, meaning "without care," originally describing church posts with no duties.

questions.q: A "perfunctory" action is one that is…
choices: Done with minimal effort or interest
questions.explication: A perfunctory glance or greeting is quick and routine, without real attention.
A recalcitrant child, or a recalcitrant mule, refuses to follow instructions.

faq: How can I improve my English vocabulary?

Read widely, keep a notebook of new words, and use them in your own sentences. Learning word roots, prefixes, and suffixes helps you guess meanings. Quizzes like this one add quick practice, and the explanations often give an example of how to use each word.
Is this vocabulary quiz good for English learners?

The first eight questions use common words and suit intermediate learners. The later ones include advanced words that even native speakers find challenging. Reading the explanations is a good way to learn how words are used in context. You can replay the quiz as often as you like.
What kinds of words does the quiz include?

The quiz mixes everyday words, synonyms and antonyms, and less common terms such as ephemeral, ubiquitous, and sycophant. The questions are designed so that there is one clearly correct meaning. Each explanation gives a little context, which makes the words easier to remember.
